Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:1.english: And in general - For one cannot say that she intends to do [him] good.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:2.hebrew: לא חיישינן - שמא תחליף ליטול היפה לעצמה:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:2.english: We do not suspect - that she might switch [the tithe-portions] in order to take the good one for herself.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:3.english: But we learned: "One who gives [dough] to his innkeeper" - [meaning he gives it to her] to prepare dough and a pot [of stew] for him.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:4.hebrew: מפני שחשודה מחלפת - והא הכא דלאו לטובה היא, דאיש נכרי הוא, ובמסכת דמאי תנינא לה, ולא קתני "המתקלקל", אלמא על הגזל חשודה:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:4.english: Because she is suspected of exchanging [it] - But here [in the case of the innkeeper] it is not for [anyone's] benefit, since he is an unrelated man; and we learn this same [teaching] in tractate Demai, and it does not teach [the case of] "the one that spoils," which shows that she is suspected of actual theft.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:5.hebrew: התם נמי מוריא כו' - התם נמי לטובה היא מתכוונת, והא דלא תנא בה המתקלקל, משום דאפילו אין מתקלקל נמי, אם נצטנן הלחם קודם שאכלו מחלפת ליה, דמוריא הוראה לעצמה: לטובה אני מתכוונת, בר בי רב ליכול חמימא כו'. אבל נותן לשכנתו, אין לה לחוש עליו, ולא מחלפת לטובה, שהרי אין סמוך עליה תמיד כאכסנאי, ולהרע נמי לא חשידא אגזל:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:1:5.english: There also, she gives a reason, etc. - There too, she intends [it] for the good. And the reason it does not state regarding it [that it is because of the bread] spoiling is that even if it does not spoil, [still,] if the bread got cold before he ate it, she switches it for him, since she has a ready justification for herself: "I intended it for the good, so that the scholar should eat it hot," etc. But one who gives [bread] to his neighbor - she need not be concerned about it, and she does not switch it for the good, since he does not rely on her constantly like a lodger; and for the bad, too, she is not suspected of theft.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:1.english: And [as for] switching [it for another loaf] - We are not concerned about theft [i.e., we assume she would not steal, only possibly switch a non-tithed loaf for a tithed one].

Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:2.english: Grinds - She [the wife of the chaver] helps operate the millstones while she [the wife of the am ha'aretz] grinds the grain of the am ha'aretz.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:3.hebrew: בזמן - שאשת חבר טמאה, ליכא למיחש שמא תשכח ותתן לתוך פיה דבר שאינו מעושר, דכיון דטמאה היא אינה רגילה ליגע במה שהיא עסוקה בו שמא תטמאה, וסתמה עומדת מרחוק היא ולא נגעה:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:3.english: When - [This explains the initial view, that] when the wife of a ḥaver is [ritually] impure, there is no need to worry that she might forget and put into her mouth something that has not been tithed, since, being impure, she is not accustomed to touch what she is engaged with, lest she render it impure; and she typically stands off at a distance and does not touch it.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:4.hebrew: אבל לא בזמן שהיא טהורה - דהואיל וסתמה נוגעת, חיישינן שמא תשכח ותאכל:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:2:4.english: But not when she is pure - Since she usually touches [the grain], we are concerned lest she forget and eat [it].

Rashi on Chullin 6b:3:1.hebrew: שחבירתה נותנת לה ואוכלת - אלמא שחשודה לגנוב משל בעלה ולהאכיל את חבירתה. ואשת חבר, אע"פ שאינה רגילה לא לאכול גזל ולא לאכול דבר שאינו מעושר, חיישינן לשכחה, דעביד אינש דמינשי ואכיל מאי דיהבי ליה, אבל לתת לאחרים, אי לאו דחשודה ורגילה בגזל, לא מינשיא:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:3:1.english: That her friend gives to her and she eats [it] - This proves that she is suspected of stealing from her husband and feeding her friend. And [as for] the wife of a chaver (a fellow scrupulous about tithes), even though she is not accustomed to eating stolen goods, nor to eating untithed produce, we are concerned about forgetfulness - for a person tends to forget and eat whatever is given to him. But as for giving to others, were she not [already] suspected and accustomed to theft, she would not forget herself [and give away stolen goods].

Rashi on Chullin 6b:4:1.english: She rules - She permits it for herself.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:4:2.english: The ox eats from what it is threshing - And this, since it assists it (i.e., this - the same one just mentioned), is not considered theft.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:1.hebrew: העיד רבי יהושע - הא נמי משום אין הקב"ה מביא תקלה על ידי הצדיקים, נקט לה:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua testified - This too, he mentions because the Holy One, blessed be He, does not bring about a stumbling-block through the righteous.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:2.english: A leaf of a vegetable - And he did not tithe [it].

Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:3.english: And Rabbi permitted [it] - on the basis of this testimony.

Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:4.hebrew: את בית שאן כולה - לאכול ירק שלה ופירות האילן בטבלן. קס"ד, קסבר רבי מאיר לאו מארץ ישראל היא, ומעשר דגן בחוצה לארץ הוא נוהג מדרבנן, הואיל ובארץ דאורייתא, אבל מעשר ירק דבארץ גופיה דרבנן, לא גזור מידי בחוצה לארץ, דאי מא"י היא, אע"ג דרבי מאיר ורבי אחר חורבן הוו, הא קיימא לן מעשר דגן דאורייתא וירק דרבנן, דקדושה אחרונה דעזרא קדשה אף לעתיד לבא, כדקתני התיר רבי את בית שאן, מכלל דשאר מקומות נוהג בהן:
Rashi on Chullin 6b:5:4.english: All of Beit Shean - to eat its vegetables and tree fruit while they are still tevel (untithed). The assumption was that Rabbi Meir held that it is not part of Eretz Yisrael, and that the tithing of grain outside the Land is observed only by rabbinic law, since in the Land it is a Torah law; but the tithing of vegetables, which even in the Land itself is only rabbinic, they did not decree anything about it outside the Land. For if it were part of Eretz Yisrael - even though Rabbi Meir and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] lived after the destruction of the Temple - we nevertheless maintain that the tithing of grain is a Torah law while [the tithing of] vegetables is rabbinic, since the later sanctification by Ezra sanctified the land even for the future, as indicated by the fact that it teaches: "Rabbi permitted [all of] Beit Shean" - implying that in the rest of the places [the obligation] does apply.

Tosafot on Chullin 6b:1:1.hebrew: התם נמי מוריא ואמרה בר בי רב ליכול חמימא ואנא איכול קרירא - פירש בקונטרס: מורה הוראת היתר לעצמה, לטובה אני מתכוונת, בר בי רב ליכול חמימא בניחותא. ואין הלשון משמע כן, דמוריא משמע שמורה לעצמה היתר לעכב משלו, כמו מוריא ואמרה תורא מדישיה קאכיל. ועוד תנן במתניתין: מעשר את שהוא נותן לה ואת שהוא נוטל הימנה, מפני שחשודה שמחלפת. רבי יוסי אומר: אין אנו אחראין לרמאים. ומפרש רבינו מנחם דבתמיה קאמר: בר בי רב ליכול חמימא ואנא איכול קרירא, ואני טרחתי בשבילו? אבל גבי שכנתו אין לחוש לחילוף, אע"פ שטורחת בשבילו, דדרך שכנים שטורחים זה בשביל זה:
Tosafot on Chullin 6b:1:1.english: There too, she also rules [a leniency] for herself and says: "Let the scholar eat hot, and I will eat cold" - Rashi explains: she issues a lenient ruling for herself, [thinking] "I intend it for the good" - "let the scholar eat hot" - stated as a plain assertion (be-nichuta), not as a question. But the language does not seem to imply this, for "moriya" (she rules) implies that she is ruling leniently for herself in order to hold back some of [the food] for herself, similar to [the expression]: "she rules and says: the ox eats from what it treads" [justifying taking a portion for herself by analogy to the law permitting a laboring animal to eat from the produce it processes]. Furthermore, we learned in the Mishnah: one must tithe both what he gives her and what he takes from her, because she is suspected of switching [the produce], [though] Rabbi Yosei says: we are not responsible for cheaters. And Rabbeinu Menachem explains that it is said as a rhetorical question: "Should the scholar eat hot while I eat cold - when I have troubled myself on his behalf?!" But with regard to her neighbor, there is no concern of switching, even though she troubles herself on the neighbor's behalf, because it is the way of neighbors to trouble themselves for one another.

Tosafot on Chullin 6b:2:1.hebrew: אשת חבר טוחנת עם אשת עם הארץ - פי' בקונטרס טוחנת תבואה של עם הארץ, בזמן שהיא טמאה אשת חבר, דליכא למיחש שמא תשכח ותתן לתוך פיה דבר שאינו מעושר, דכיון דטמאה היא אינה נוגעת, ומסתמא עומדת מרחוק. וקשה, דהך משנה מתניא במסכת טהרות (פ"ז), ולפי' הקונטרס הוה ליה למיתני במסכ' דמאי. ועוד קשה, דפי' דחברתה נותנת לה ואוכלת, אלמא חשודה לגנוב משל בעלה, ואין זה גזלה, דאין הבעל מקפיד בדבר מועט, כדתנן בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיט.): "מקבלין מן הנשים דבר מועט לצדקה". וגם זה דוחק מאד, שמחלק בין אשת חבר לאשת עם הארץ, דעביד איניש דמינשי ואכיל מה דיהבי ליה, אבל לתת לאחרים, אי לאו דרגילה בגזל, לא מינשיא. ועוד, היאך טוחנת עמה אשת חבר, הרי היא מסייעת עוברי עבירה. ובסוף הניזקין (גיטין דף סא.) מוכח דאסור לרבא, דמפרש מתניתין דמשאלת אשת חבר לאשת עם הארץ נפה וכברה ובוררת וטוחנת עמה, בעם הארץ דרבי מאיר, וטומאה וטהרה דרבנן, אבל בסתם עם הארץ לא, כי היכי דלא תטחון עם חברתה החשודה על השביעית. ולאביי, דאמר רוב עמי הארץ מעשרין הן, שרי לסייעה בכל ענין. והכא הא אסרינן בזמן שהיא טהורה, וליכא לאוקומי ההיא בזמן שהיא טמאה ודלא כרבי שמעון בן אלעזר, דהא בהדיא קתני בוררת, ובוררת נוגעת היא. ומפרש ר"ח וכן ר"ת, שבתבואה של [חבר] איירי בזמן שהיא טמאה, בזמן שאשת עם הארץ מחזקת עצמה כטמאה, שאז היא נזהרת מליגע בתבואה, אבל לא בזמן שמחזקת עצמה בטהורה, דאז אין נזהרת מליגע בתבואה ומטמאה לה. "רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר: אף בזמן שמחזקת עצמה בחזקת טמאה לא תטחון, מפני שחברתה אשת עם הארץ, אחר שסבורה להיות טהורה, נותנת לה ואוכלת". ובתוספתא דטהרות פ"ח קתני: "אע"פ שאינה אוכלת, נותנת לאחרים ואוכלים". והשתא פריך שפיר, השתא מגזל גזלה, תבואה של אשת חבר חילופי מיבעיא:
Tosafot on Chullin 6b:2:1.english: The wife of a chaver may grind [grain] together with the wife of an am ha'aretz - Rashi explains: she may grind the grain of the am ha'aretz while she, the wife of the chaver, is ritually impure (temeah), for there is no concern that she might forget and put into her mouth something that is not tithed, since, being impure, she does not touch [the grain], and presumably she stands off at a distance. This is difficult, for this mishnah is taught in Tractate Taharot (chapter 7), whereas according to Rashi's explanation it ought to have been taught in Tractate Demai. And it is further difficult, for he explains that her fellow (the wife of the am ha'aretz) gives to her and she eats - implying that the wife of the am ha'aretz is suspected of stealing from her husband, and that this is not [considered] outright theft (gezeilah), since the husband does not mind about a small amount, as we learn in the last chapter of "HaGozel" (Bava Kamma 119a): "we accept a small amount from women for charity." And this too is a great difficulty, for it draws a distinction between the wife of the chaver and the wife of the am ha'aretz: a person is prone to forget and eat what is given to him, but as for giving to others - were she not already accustomed to theft, she would not forget [that it is wrong]. And furthermore, how could the wife of the chaver grind together with her? She would be aiding transgressors! And at the end of "HaNizakin" (Gittin 61a) it is proven that this is forbidden according to Rava, who explains the mishnah there - that the wife of a chaver may lend the wife of an am ha'aretz a sieve and a sifter, and may sort [grain] and grind with her - as referring to an am ha'aretz in accordance with Rabbi Meir['s view], where the concern of impurity and purity is only rabbinic (derabbanan); but not with an ordinary am ha'aretz, so that she should not [thereby come to] grind with her fellow who is suspect regarding produce of the sabbatical year (sheviit). And according to Abaye, who says that most amei ha'aretz do tithe, it is permitted to assist her in every respect. But here [in our mishnah] we forbid it while she [the wife of the chaver] is pure (tehorah), and one cannot establish that [ruling in Gittin] as referring to a time when she is impure, and as not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar - for it explicitly teaches "sorts" (boreret), and one who sorts does touch [the grain]. And Rabbeinu Chananel, and likewise Rabbeinu Tam, explain that with regard to the grain of [the chaver], [our mishnah] deals with a time when she [the wife of the chaver] is impure - specifically, at a time when the wife of the am ha'aretz considers herself impure, for then she is careful not to touch the grain; but not at a time when she considers herself pure, for then she is not careful about touching the grain, and she renders it impure for her [the wife of the chaver]. "Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: even at a time when she [the wife of the am ha'aretz] holds herself to be impure, [the wife of the chaver] should not grind [with her], because her fellow, the wife of the am ha'aretz, once she comes to believe that she has become pure, gives to her and eats." And in the Tosefta of Taharot, chapter 8, it teaches: "even though she does not eat [it herself], she gives it to others and they eat it." And now the question is well-founded: since she is prone to outright steal the grain of the wife of the chaver, is there [even] need to ask about switching [untithed produce for tithed]?
